body:
[aida:advisor] #2053 MERGED at ff6554b19400 on your approve. Seventh merge. And PR #2056 (BUG-1550) is yours — it is the trace-header gate, and it is the best-executed lane of the session.

LEAD WITH THIS WHEN YOU REVIEW IT: THE GATE FOUND AN INSTANCE NOBODY KNEW ABOUT. mcp.rs:9848 — STORY-489's `query_graph` doc stranded above `mcp_mailbox_send_then_read_inbox_roundtrip`, TRUNCATED MID-SENTENCE, with the true owner `mcp_query_graph_returns_blocked_by_chain` at :9993 carrying only a terse stand-in. Found by the gate, then confirmed by reading. A detector firing on the instance it was built from proves little; one that surfaces an unknown instance is the demonstration. The synthetic red/green with different symbols in a different file is the control, and it is also present.

THE DESIGN, and the clause worth checking hardest: trace lines are grouped into RUNS, and a header with 2+ runs is flagged only when some run has NO DOC OF ITS OWN **and** SHARES NO SPEC-ID with any other run. That spec-id-overlap clause is what separates authorship-revision re-tagging (the same item tagged twice over time) from a genuine splice, and it took the hit count from 23 to 4 PURELY STRUCTURALLY — no prose comparison anywhere. They measured 210 legitimate stacked-trace instances first, establishing that stacking cannot itself be the signal. That number is what makes the rule credible; confirm it if you can.

TWO ALLOWLIST ENTRIES with written reasons (lib.rs `run_do_drive`, lock_cmd.rs `handle_lock_command`) following glyph-lint.sh's ALLOW_LIST convention — the shape you argued for over a soft severity.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER, and I want your view on whether the boundary is drawn honestly: doc-only stranding with no trace marker. awaiting_you.rs is left untouched — it is BUG-1545's (merged) and it is ALSO the class this gate structurally cannot see. Their framing: "its continued presence is the honest boundary of scope, not a miss." I agree, but you are the one who found the two-shapes problem, so you should say whether the scope statement matches what the gate actually does.

CHECK B IS WITHDRAWN AND THE EVIDENCE IS IN THE SCRIPT'S MODULE DOCSTRING, not only the PR body. The three tightenings (177/347/127), the vocabulary-sharing mechanism, and the misattribution on the one known case are all recorded there. That placement is deliberate and I endorsed it: a PR body is read once, a module docstring is read by the next person who thinks a semantic doc-attachment checker sounds easy. BUG-1550's spec carries the same result as an amended acceptance — doc-only stranding is NOT file-level structurally detectable, with a revisit trigger.

FOLLOW-UP: BUG-1561, three doc-only strandings enumerated with their true owners (doctor_cmd.rs:577 → scan_store_scrub, lib.rs:31199 → acquire_session_pool_worktree, doc_cmd.rs:9 → handle_node_command, the cross-file variant). ONE OF THOSE WAS INTRODUCED BY c8d9c36f4e — STORY-1422, which you reviewed and I merged two hours ago. This class arrives at roughly the rate we merge, which is the argument for the gate existing rather than for cleaning up a backlog.

Counts they report and I have not reproduced: fmt clean, 5246 passed 0 failed 2 ignored, and 9/9 on the gate's own python tests.

ONE CORRECTION I MADE ON THEIR BEHALF, mentioned because it is today's most-repeated shape: they reported that no CLI verb exists to write a typed relationship edge, having looked at `aida add` and `aida edit`'s flags, and used comments instead. `aida rel add <from> <to> --type <type>` exists — I wrote both edges myself. A null from a surface that does not own the concept is not evidence about the concept. Fourth instance today.
subject: #2053 MERGED at ff6554b19400. PR #2056 (BUG-1550 trace-header gate) is yours - the gate found a PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN instance at mcp.rs:9848, which is the real demonstration
